title: Analysis of the frequency shift in coherent population trapping resonance's dynamic continuous-wave spectroscopy at the phase-jump modulation and its comparison with the conventional approach
authors: E. D. Chivilis, E. A. Tsygankov
abstract: We present the research of dynamic continuous-wave spectroscopy of the coherent population trapping resonance at the phase-jump modulation. Λ system of levels supplemented by a nonabsorbing state and bichromatic optical field, whose spectral components have different intensities, are considered. We demonstrate that the asymmetry leads to an additional nonlinear shift of the error-signal frequency under unisotropic relaxation of the ground-state density-matrix elements. We also investigate the conventional approach where the frequency difference of the optical field components is harmonically modulated to obtain the error signal. Comparison demonstrates that in the high-frequency modulation regime the corresponding frequency shift is more linear than at the phase-jump modulation for nonshort integration times.
summary: This paper theoretically compares the frequency shift measured in CPT resonance using phase-jump modulation versus conventional harmonic modulation. The authors derive and analyze the error signal shift for both methods under a $\Lambda$-system model. They conclude that while mathematically similar at short times, the conventional method is preferred experimentally due to its superior noise performance at higher frequencies.
main_problem: The study compares the frequency shift observed in coherent population trapping (CPT) resonance spectroscopy when using phase-jump modulation versus conventional harmonic sinusoidal modulation.
main_result: While both techniques yield similar results at short integration times, the authors conclude that the conventional approach is more suitable for light shift suppression due to its ability to operate at higher frequencies and better noise characteristics.
method: The analysis involves solving the quantum Liouville equation under various approximations (e.g., low saturation) and deriving expressions for the error signal shift ($\delta_{as}$ or $\delta_Q$) for both modulation schemes.
model_or_system: The system is a three-level Lambda ($\Lambda$) configuration driven by a bichromatic optical field, modeled using a Hamiltonian and governed by the quantum Liouville equation. The analysis focuses on ground-state density matrix elements.
key_observables: Frequency shift of the error signal ($\delta_{as}$ or $\delta_Q$), which is derived from the difference in absorption measurements.
important_parameters: Integration time ($	au$), modulation parameters ($m, \omega_m$), and relaxation rates ($\Gamma_c, \Gamma_g$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes unisotropic relaxation for ground-state elements and neglects Doppler broadening compared to the homogeneous width.
figures_summary: Figures compare the frequency shift ($\delta_{tot}(	au)$) vs. integration time $	au$, showing agreement between techniques at short times, and plot the dependence of the normalized slope on the parameter $ eta$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory for both phase-jump spectroscopy and conventional harmonic modulation separately before performing a detailed comparison of the resulting frequency shift formulas and numerical results across varying parameters.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical comparison between two advanced spectroscopic techniques used to measure fundamental properties (like light shifts) in atomic systems, which is highly relevant for experimental quantum optics research.
